rules.description: Flags an agent turn that starts too long after the customer finished speaking.
known_limits: Only as accurate as the timestamps you supply.
Measures customer end to next agent start, only for a customer turn followed directly by an agent turn.
Overlapping turns (a negative gap) are skipped, not counted as latency.
The default thresholds are not checked against what callers actually notice.
rules.name: High latency
needs: start_ms and end_ms on both turns of a customer-to-agent pair
rules.severity: Medium above the base threshold, high above the high threshold.

rules.description: Flags an agent turn that says (almost) the same thing as the agent's previous turn.
known_limits: Compares only with the previous agent turn.
Compares sets of words, so word order is ignored and different sentences with the same words can match.
Splits text on spaces, so languages written without spaces are not handled.
A deliberate repeat, such as reading back an order number, is flagged too.
rules.name: Repeated agent turn

rules.applies_to: Agents whose name starts with restaurant or hotel
rules.description: Flags an agent confirmation that contradicts what the customer just asked for: a different quantity, a non-vegetarian item for a vegetarian request, an excluded ingredient, or a smoking room for a non-smoking request.
known_limits: Only runs for agent names starting with restaurant or hotel.
Uses small English word lists: quantities 1 to 20, vegetarian words, a few excluded items and non-smoking.
Only checks the first agent turn with a confirmation word before the next customer turn.
Findings are candidates for review, not verdicts: the customer may have changed the request later.
rules.name: Ignored constraint
rules.severity: High for dietary, exclusion and smoking contradictions, medium for a quantity mismatch.

rules.description: Flags an agent turn that claims success right after a tool call failed.
known_limits: Needs tool_events. CSV imports and phone calls have none, so this rule cannot run on them.
Only checks the first agent turn after a failed tool event.
Matches a short English phrase list and skips turns containing a negation word such as sorry or not.
Cannot tell whether a later tool call succeeded.
rules.name: False success claim

rules.description: Flags an agent turn that starts while the customer's previous turn was still going.
known_limits: The 500 ms default is a guess, not a measured value.
Only as accurate as the timestamps you supply. Speech-to-text timestamps can be rough, so normal turn-taking may look like an overlap.
Only checks an agent turn that directly follows a customer turn. A customer interrupting the agent is not flagged.
Cannot tell a short acknowledgement from talking over the customer.
rules.name: Agent talking over customer
needs: start_ms and end_ms on both turns of a customer-to-agent pair

rules.description: Flags a customer turn that says (almost) the same thing as the customer's previous turn, which can mean the agent missed it.
known_limits: Compares only with the previous customer turn.
Skips turns shorter than 3 words, so a repeat like yes please is not caught.
Compares sets of words, so a rephrased repeat can score below the default and be missed.
Splits text on spaces, so languages written without spaces are not handled.
The customer may repeat themselves for other reasons, such as a bad line or a repeated question from the agent.
rules.name: Customer repeated themselves
